pairs.why: B's truss runs off the frame diagonally and is cropped like the real card, while A shows a short, flat front-on truss bar that reads as a separate toy object.
A is turned three-quarter and shows more of the seat's top face, close to the real card's high camera, while B is more frontal with a thinner seat.
B is tilted and turned with some perspective, like the real cards' angled objects, while A is a dead-flat symmetric front view.
A's coils are seen from a higher three-quarter angle and float on the backdrop like the real objects, while B sits on a ground shadow with a side-on view.
A keeps a simple wall behind the target and bear with a shelf top visible, like the real card, while B adds clutter props and a busy brick wall that crowd the depth layers.
B is seen from slightly above with the cap top showing and a rounded base, like the real bottle, while A shows the bottom ellipse from below, so its camera conflicts with the cap view.
B has a higher camera with the tracks receding diagonally and a readable ground plane, closer to the real cards' high views, while A is low and front-on with tracks running flat across.
A has a higher camera with the horizon near the top and water filling most of the frame, like the real card, while B shows a lower, more distant horizon and a wider view.
